newsitem.title: ROMANIA: President says Romania will enter NATO next time.
newsitem.headline: President says Romania will enter NATO next time.

text.p: President Emil Constantinescu said Romania had made progress in proving to NATO leaders that it was worthy of joining the Alliance and would work hard to secure membership in the next wave of new admissions.

"It could have been better, just as it could have been worse," Constantinescu told a television interviewer late on Tuesday after NATO leaders in Madrid passed over Romania for the first expansion, taking in only Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.

"What's important now is that all participants said they appreciated the progress made by Romania. This means we must go on. We have proceeded with reforms and turned Romania into a pillar of regional stability."

Romania's leaders gracefully admitted after the Madrid decision that their bid for early membership had been thwarted by the gap in economic progress separating the country from the three successful entrants.

U.S. President Bill Clinton is due to visit Romania on Friday and offer encouragement to the Balkan country to pursue the economic reforms undertaken since Constantinescu and his centrist allies won elections last November.

Western countries have applauded the government's programme aimed at recovering lost ground from seven years of sluggish reform by ex-communists who took power after the 1989 removal of dictator Nicolae Ceausescu.
Constantinescu said the mention of Romania, along with Slovenia, as prime candidates for future expansion was a key consideration in eventually joining the Alliance.
"This means that if we continue on this track until 1999, we'll get the place we deserve," he said.
Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea told a Romanian television station that being overlooked for initial entry was no tragedy.
"We should not be looking for culprits," he said. "The best thing for us now is to look to the future, to concentrate on what we have to do."
